end.summary:
Interpreted position-time graphs as motion stories using cycling and signal examples.
Read slope of an x-t graph as velocity and linked steeper lines with greater speed.
Calculated velocity as 30/10 = 3 m/s and acceleration as (10−0)/5 = 2 m/s².
Identified a horizontal x-t line as an object at rest; no misconceptions recorded.
end.parentNote: Asha practised reading position-time graphs, using slope to compare velocity, and calculating velocity and acceleration. Ira explained the method with cycling examples and correctly applied distance ÷ time and change in velocity ÷ time. They repeated that a horizontal line on a position-time graph means the object is stopped; the lesson did not include a later correction of a mix-up. At home, ask Ira to describe one graph as a motion story and state what its slope means.
